title: LeanDojo: Theorem Proving with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
abstract: LeanDojo is an open-source toolkit for theorem proving with retrieval-augmented language models. It extracts data from Lean and enables interaction with the proof environment programmatically. LeanDojo introduces ReProver, a retrieval-augmented prover that selects premises from a vast math library.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to prove a mathematical theorem. You start with a goal and apply tactics to simplify it, until you reach a solution. Retrieval-augmented language models can help with this process by selecting relevant premises from a large math library.

This approach is similar to how you would use a search engine to find relevant information when working on a problem.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
LeanDojo extracts data from Lean, including file dependencies, abstract syntax trees, states, tactics, and premises. This data is used to train ReProver, which generates tactics conditioning on a small number of retrieved premises.

The retriever uses program analysis to identify accessible premises and hard negative examples.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
The LeanDojo Benchmark contains 98,734 theorems and proofs extracted from Lean's math library. ReProver achieves a proof rate of 51.2%, outperforming a baseline that generates tactics directly without retrieval (47.6%) and another baseline using GPT-4 to generate tactics in a zero-shot manner (29.0%).

These results demonstrate the effectiveness of ReProver in theorem proving.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Theorem proving is a challenging task that requires reasoning and problem-solving skills. By developing effective retrieval-augmented language models like ReProver, we can improve the state-of-the-art in theorem proving and make it more accessible to researchers and practitioners.

This can have significant implications for fields like mathematics, computer science, and formal verification.

config.title: Impact of Theorem Proving on Related Fields

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
LeanDojo introduces several key innovations, including program analysis for identifying accessible premises, in-file negatives for training the retriever, and a challenging benchmark for evaluating theorem provers.

These innovations enable ReProver to achieve state-of-the-art results in theorem proving.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
LeanDojo is an open-source toolkit that can be used by researchers and practitioners to develop and evaluate their own theorem provers.

By trying out LeanDojo, you can explore the capabilities of retrieval-augmented language models in theorem proving and contribute to the development of this exciting field.
